rationale: The claim concerns Figure 9's regression of average employment growth on relative MANUFACTURING wages, 1950-90 (slope -0.68, t=0.6). The run could not reconstruct this: manufacturing production-worker AHE (SIC basis, 1947-1990) is flagged as not reconstructable from free modern APIs, so results/persistence_convergence.json reports mfg_wage_convergence_* = None and mfg_wage_convergence_note. What was actually produced (empgrowth_vs_relwage_slope=0.00164, empgrowth_vs_relwage_t=0.164, per its note) is a documented PROXY: employment growth 1970-90 regressed on mean relative per-capita income 1970-90 — a different variable (income, not mfg wages) over a different window (1970-90, not 1950-90). No output/figures/figure9.pdf was generated (only fig1,2,4,7,11,13,14 exist under figures/). Numerically the produced values do not match the paper's: the slope (0.0016) is a different sign and magnitude in incomparable units, and the t-stat (0.16) is ~4x smaller than 0.6 (well outside the 30% partial band). The proxy does qualitatively echo the paper's central point — 'essentially no relationship' (t well below significance) — but the specific scalar values of the manufacturing-wage regression could not be reproduced.
